evidence.role: Permissionless settlement entrypoint delegates to the storage allocator without an actor check.
Redemption requires the current ticket owner and provisionally consumes the claim before delivery.
Both delivery branches revert on observable failure after provisional claim-state changes.
Inherited implementation performs the ticket burn and rejects a nonexistent claim.
Cash-delivery failure becomes a revert; the underlying helper also bubbles token reverts.

searched.where: All five production Solidity files and all dependencies listed in target/dependency-hashes.json
searched.result: Read completely; 31 dependencies enumerated and all 31 recomputed SHA-256 values matched.
2 hits: IRaffle ABI declaration and Raffle implementation; no in-scope wrapper or caller.
5 hits: ABI declaration, external entrypoint, two private-helper calls, and private helper definition.
0 hits; delivery failures are not caught or converted to success.
3 hits: inherited definition, winning redemption, and the separate Refunding-only ticket-refund path.
2 hits: IERC721 declaration and inherited ERC721 implementation; Raffle has no ownerOf override.

reasoning: Standalone settlement has no identity gate and its complete NFT/cash branches only validate and allocate local liabilities. Redemption requires msg.sender to equal inherited ownerOf(ticketId), burns the ticket, and then performs NFT or cash delivery. NFT call/read failures and ownership mismatch revert; SafeERC20 bubbles or raises cash-transfer failure; no catch path exists, so same-call settlement, flags, accounting, burn, token effects, and logs roll back. Both result branches enforce the property, making this implemented rather than partial. Confidence is medium because concrete deployed prize and quote-token implementations are outside the frozen target and could falsely report success.
